specification.family_title: Connection recovery and unsafe pool reuse
specification.title: The top-level ROLLBACK of a failed transaction fails on the client; then the next unit of work runs on the same pool
steps: Unit 1: start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API, on a pool of one connection.
Checkpoint `unit1-after-write`: report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid(). Then arm the client-side fault: the next top-level ROLLBACK fails in the driver and is not sent.
Raise an application error inside the transaction. The framework attempts ROLLBACK, which fails, so the connection keeps its open transaction.
When the fault fires, before the framework sees its error, the adapter's driver layer reports checkpoint `after-fault` (the backend PID): the runner records the fault's effect on the server.
Checkpoint `after-unit1`: report the same backend PID; the runner records that session's state.

Unit 2, the next unit of work on the same pool: start a transaction, write the marker `next`, checkpoint `unit2-after-write` (report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid()), and end normally. Give up after settings.bound_ms and report the unit as pending.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: Unrelated work never runs inside, or commits, a transaction whose rollback failed: that transaction is never committed, and the next unit of work runs in a transaction of its own.
After the failure, the next unit of work on the same pool completes within the bound (settings.bound_ms) and commits.

execution.description: Declarative @Transactional through TransactionInterceptor, on HikariCP 7.1.0 with maximumPoolSize 1. No other pool setting is changed. The statement-error case uses rollbackFor = Exception.class so the checked SQLException takes the rollback path the case describes. The default rule, which does not roll back a checked exception, is not used for that case.

configuration.rollbackRule: default RuntimeException and Error; TX-03.statement-error-rollback-not-sent uses rollbackFor Exception.class

execution.form: Declarative: the call goes through a JDK proxy and TransactionInterceptor. PROPAGATION_REQUIRED. Writes are PreparedStatement calls on the connection DataSourceUtils.getConnection returns.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A client-side injection in the adapter's driver layer (node-postgres, pg.Client.prototype.query): the top-level ROLLBACK fails without being sent, as a failed send would.
fault.preconditions: The framework's statements pass through the instrumented pg module (recorded as trace_sees_framework_pg).
fault.expected_server: Unit 1's transaction stays open on its connection ("idle in transaction"), holding the doomed write.
fault.expected_client: An error from the framework's rollback; what the framework then does with the connection is under test.

knowledge: The framework knows that its ROLLBACK failed, so it knows that the connection's transaction state is unknown.

api_outcome.basis: the @Transactional proxy threw a throwable the method did not throw
api_outcome.contract: Spring Framework 7.0.9 @Transactional methods run through TransactionInterceptor (org.springframework.transaction.interceptor.TransactionAspectSupport.completeTransactionAfterThrowing). The call is on a JDK proxy. The target is not invoked directly. If TransactionAttribute.rollbackOn returns true, the interceptor calls PlatformTransactionManager.rollback and rethrows the application throwable. If rollback throws TransactionSystemException, that exception replaces the application throwable and initApplicationException stores the original. If rollbackOn returns false, the interceptor calls commit. With no rollbackFor rules, RuleBasedTransactionAttribute.rollbackOn delegates to DefaultTransactionAttribute.rollbackOn, which is true for RuntimeException and Error only. The 7.0.9 reference, Rolling Back a Declarative Transaction, states: "In its default configuration, the Spring Framework's transaction infrastructure code marks a transaction for rollback only in the case of runtime, unchecked exceptions. That is, when the thrown exception is an instance or subclass of RuntimeException. (Error instances also, by default, result in a rollback)." A normal return is reported as committed. The method's own throwable leaving the proxy is reported as rolled_back. Any other throwable leaving the proxy is reported as failed. Propagation.NESTED, Spring Framework 7.0.9: "Execute within a nested transaction if a current transaction exists, behave like REQUIRED otherwise." DataSourceTransactionManager's class javadoc says nestedTransactionAllowed defaults to true and nested transactions use JDBC savepoints. Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW: "Create a new transaction, and suspend the current transaction if one exists." The statement-error case uses rollbackFor = Exception.class so a checked SQLException takes the rollback path that case describes. The default rule would commit on that checked exception. That default is not substituted for the case.

error.message: JDBC rollback failed: application error: unit 1 fails: injected client-side failure: ROLLBACK was not sent

evaluation.reason: TX-03.1 violated: failed transaction: xid 9506 committed at report time (`after-unit1`); doomed visible: true; next unit's transaction: 9507

preconditions.description: the write of marker "doomed" had reached PostgreSQL at `unit1-after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the write of marker "next" had reached PostgreSQL at `unit2-after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the client-side fault (client-reject) fired exactly once
the next unit of work was attempted
the withheld ROLLBACK left unit 1's transaction open: its session was in a transaction holding unit 1's ID
preconditions.detail: at `after-fault`: session "idle in transaction", backend_xid 9506; transactionid locks [9506]
